# TDPdf v1.26.0.0

**The zoom storm is over, text boxes can be styled, and reordering pages works the way the sidebar always implied it did.**

## The storm, and the comment that hid it

A handler sat on WPF's `DpiChanged` event under a confident note explaining that it never fires — that TDPdf's own `WM_DPICHANGED` hook claims the message first, so this was harmless dead code kept only for the day WPF might raise the event.

WPF raises the event. The `Zoom.Churn` diagnostic added in 1.25.0.0 said so on the first report back, and then again from a second, unrelated machine: **13 full zoom passes a second, sustained for two seconds.** Each one cancelled and restarted a page render, re-fitted the view, and wrote a settings file to disk. That is the churn behind the text-box failures chased across five releases, and it had been hiding behind a paragraph of prose asserting it could not happen.

The handler stays, because it demonstrably *is* a live DPI path on some machines and deleting it would trade a storm for a stale page. It now does something only when the DPI has actually changed — which is what makes "idempotent" true rather than merely hoped for.

Two days and three releases of instrumentation to find; four lines to fix. Worth remembering which of those was the hard part.

## Bold, italic and underline in text boxes

**Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+U while editing.** They were listed in the shortcut overlay and did nothing — the same thing upstream found in their own build.

This is more than a keybinding: text annotations carried a size and a colour and nothing else. Everything that measures text now shares one typeface — the box on screen, the annotation measurement, the wrap calculation and the PDF burn-in — because bold and italic change glyph advances, and if those four disagree the text moves at the moment you save it. Underline is drawn explicitly, because the font-style flag for it exists in the PDF library and the library's own draw call ignores it, so an underlined note would have looked right on screen and saved without the line.

Notes you have already made are untouched: all three default to off.

Inside a text box Ctrl+I is italic; everywhere else it still toggles night mode. That split is deliberate, and the shortcut overlay now says so.

## Pages drag as a block

The Pages sidebar has always allowed selecting a run of pages, and dragging then moved exactly one of them. It now moves the whole selection, in order, carrying each page's rotation, and leaves the block selected where it lands so a second drag starts from where you are already looking.

A **two-pixel accent line** shows precisely which gap the pages will drop into rather than asking you to infer it from the cursor. The line and the reorder read the same calculation, so the indicator cannot promise somewhere the pages do not go.

And dropping a block back where it started is now correctly nothing at all. It used to rewrite and reload the document anyway — which discards unsaved annotations, the documented cost of any structural page edit — in exchange for no change whatsoever.

## What is deliberately still out

Two upstream features were assessed for this release and held back, with the reasoning recorded in issue #135.

**Letter spacing** cannot be previewed honestly. WPF has no letter-spacing primitive, so the editor would show unspaced text that rearranged itself the moment you saved — the exact failure the shared-typeface work above exists to prevent. It is worth doing properly, which means not doing it beside four other changes.

**The measurement tool** needs a new toolbar glyph, and this project builds on a machine that cannot render one to check. A blank square in the toolbar is worse than a missing feature.

Two further upstream items turned out not to apply: TDPdf already switches to a drag cursor while panning, and it has no page-duplication command whose selection could be wrong.

## What this changes for administrators

**The Intune detection rule now requires 1.26.0.0, so managed machines pick this up on the next evaluation. Assignments are unaffected.** No telemetry, policy or privacy changes in this release — the `Update.*` events and the update check introduced in 1.25.0.0 are unchanged, and this is the first release those machines will see them fire against.
